chains.title: The mutant promoter creates a GABPA-responsive TERT site
chains.element: The TERT promoter hotspot acts as a mutant-allele ETS-family binding element.

links.claim: GABPA is the leading candidate because the C250T hotspot is known to create an ETS-family site with mutant-allele binding; the case supplies no QBiC-SELEX result or occupancy data to confirm GABPA at this site.
The altered TERT promoter sequence increases the likelihood of GABPA binding and functions as a cis-regulatory element.
GABPA binding at the mutant promoter increases TERT transcription in cis.
This effect occurs in glioblastoma tumor cells, the expression context specified for the case.
Increased TERT expression supports telomerase activity and tumor-cell persistence, contributing to glioblastoma.

predictions: In a heterozygous tumor model, GABPA occupancy is greater at the alt allele than at the ref allele.
Disrupting GABPA binding reduces mutant-allele TERT transcription.
falsified_if: Allele-specific occupancy assays show no GABPA enrichment at the alt allele despite adequate assay sensitivity.
Selective disruption of GABPA does not reduce TERT expression attributable to the mutant promoter.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: The variant does not cause reproducible allele-specific TF occupancy or a cis change in TERT expression.
Any association with tumor phenotype could instead reflect a linked cause, another mechanism, or no causal effect.
falsified_if: A reproducible alt-allele-specific TF occupancy difference is shown to cause a cis increase in TERT expression.

chains.title: A different ETS factor drives the mutant promoter
chains.element: The TERT promoter hotspot acts as a mutant-allele ETS-family binding element.

links.claim: ETS1 is an alternative ETS-family candidate that could bind the created motif more strongly on the alt allele; the case supplies no ETS1 occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result.
The altered TERT promoter sequence creates or strengthens an ETS-responsive cis-regulatory element.
ETS1 binding at the mutant promoter increases TERT transcription in cis.
This effect occurs in glioblastoma tumor cells.
Increased TERT expression supports telomerase activity and tumor-cell persistence, contributing to glioblastoma.

predictions: In a heterozygous tumor model, ETS1 occupancy is greater at the alt allele than at the ref allele.
Disrupting ETS1 binding reduces mutant-allele TERT transcription, whereas disrupting GABPA has a smaller effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific occupancy assays show no ETS1 enrichment at the alt allele despite adequate assay sensitivity.
Selective disruption of ETS1 does not reduce TERT expression attributable to the mutant promoter.

matrix.test: Allele-specific CUT&RUN or ChIP-qPCR for GABPA and ETS1 in a heterozygous TERT-promoter-mutant glioblastoma model

outcomes.outcome: Alt-allele GABPA enrichment exceeds ETS1 enrichment.
Alt-allele ETS1 enrichment exceeds GABPA enrichment.
Neither factor shows reproducible alt-allele enrichment.

next_experiment: Perform allele-specific CUT&RUN or ChIP-qPCR for GABPA and ETS1 in a heterozygous TERT-promoter-mutant glioblastoma model, using matched input and allele-aware quantification. This is a low-cost way to distinguish the leading GABPA chain from the ETS1 alternative; occupancy alone would not establish the downstream TERT-expression or disease effects.
